To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
older adults have a deficit in attentional suppression (as indexed by P1 latency) and in semantic encoding (as indexed by N2 latency) during a modified Sternburg word recognition task.
aging is associated with decrements in both attentional suppression and semantic encoding, and that these decrements are indexed by P1 latency and P2 latency, respectively.
aging affects the efficiency of attentional suppression and the efficiency of encoding operations, and that these effects are reflected in the ERP components P1 and P3, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of attention in cognitive aging.
the relationship of aging to the neural mechanisms underlying cognitive processing, and in particular, the mechanisms underlying attention, encoding, and working memory.
the effects of aging on cognitive processing and the use of electrophysiological techniques to measure the effects of aging in cognitive processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ERP measures are a valuable tool to investigate age related changes in cognition.
the ERP measures in this study indicate that both attention and encoding deficits are present in aging.

the P1 latency is a marker of age-related attentional suppression, and P2 latency is a marker for semantic operations during encoding, and that both of these measures may be related to age-related cognitive decrements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging affects both attention and working-memory encoding, and these two processes interact to produce cognitive deficits.
aging is associated with a decrease in the efficiency of attentional processes and an increase in the inefficiency of memory encoding processes.

aging affects both the early stages of visual processing and the later stages of memory encoding, which are reflected in the ERP measures P1, N1 and P2, and that the P1 and P1 latency measures from appropriate visual ERP paradigms may serve as useful markers of the aging process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ERP measures can provide useful information regarding the nature of age-related cognitive deficits.
the P1-N1-P2 complex may be a useful ERP index of age-related decrements in attentional suppression and semantic encoding.
the P2 latency is a marker of the age-related decline of the encoding processes, and the P2 amplitude is a marker of attention.
